blocks.text: Painting and Branding: Why the Right Exterior Colors Can Boost Foot Traffic & Brand Identity

Whether you run a retail shop, restaurant, clinic, or commercial office space, the exterior of your building plays a powerful role in shaping how customers perceive your business before they ever walk through the door. One of the most subtle but significant factors in this perception? Color.

At Black Pearl Painters, we’ve seen firsthand how smart, strategic exterior painting can elevate a brand, increase foot traffic, and create a consistent customer experience. In this post, we’re diving into the psychology of color, branding through paint, and how your building’s look can shape your business success across Tacoma, Puyallup, and surrounding cities in Northwest Washington.
The Psychology of Color in Business

Color has a psychological impact on consumers, evoking emotions, influencing decisions, and setting expectations. In fact, research shows that people form first impressions within 90 seconds, and up to 90% of that impression is based on color alone.
Here’s how some of the most commonly used exterior colors influence perception:

items: Red: Energy, urgency, and excitement. Often used in fast food, fitness, and retail.
Blue: Trust, calm, and professionalism. Common in medical offices, banks, and tech companies.
Green: Health, balance, and growth. A favorite among health food stores, spas, and environmentally friendly brands.
Yellow: Optimism, friendliness, and youth. Used by creative brands and children’s retailers.
Black/Grey: Sophistication, power, and exclusivity. Works well for upscale boutiques or law offices.
White: Cleanliness, simplicity, and modernity. Great for dental offices, wellness centers, and minimalist brands.

blocks.text: Choosing the right color for your business exterior is about more than taste, it’s about strategy.

blocks.text: Exterior Colors That Boost Foot Traffic
When people pass your storefront or commercial building, they make instant judgments: “Is that place inviting?” “Do I trust that business?” “Does this look high-end or budget?”
A bold or cohesive exterior color scheme can dramatically increase walk-in traffic by:

items: Catching attention from drivers and pedestrians
Creating emotional resonance with your brand message
Signaling your type of business to customers who are seeking your services

blocks.text: Example 1: Boutique Bakery in Downtown Tacoma

A pastel pink and cream façade with soft gold trim instantly communicates “sweet, feminine, and inviting” perfect for a bakery that sells cupcakes, macarons, and specialty coffee. The color scheme turns heads and invites passersby to snap photos or stop in for a treat.
Example 2: Fitness Center in Puyallup

A combination of dark charcoal and bright red conveys strength, energy, and power ideal for a high-intensity gym. The contrast makes the building pop, and the red adds a sense of urgency that drives action.
Example 3: Holistic Wellness Spa in Gig Harbor
Earthy greens and off-whites communicate tranquility and balance, appealing to customers looking for peace, wellness, and a natural vibe.
Each of these examples shows how strategic color can send the right message and make your building a local landmark.
Consistency = Brand Recognition
Your building’s exterior is part of your overall branding, just like your logo, website, and signage. Consistent use of colors across all platforms builds recognition and trust.
Think of:

items: Starbucks: That iconic green is on signs, storefronts, cups, and even uniforms.
McDonald’s: The red and yellow combo is recognized globally.
UPS: “What can Brown do for you?” isn’t just a slogan, it’s a brand identity.

blocks.text: Even if you’re a small business, matching your exterior paint colors to your brand palette reinforces your professionalism and improves brand recall. Whether you’re rebranding or launching a new location, an exterior paint update can be the visual reset that brings your image together.

Mistakes to Avoid When Painting Your Business Exterior
Choosing Trendy Colors That Don’t Fit Your Brand
Just because sage green is trending doesn’t mean it suits your automotive repair shop. Stay true to your brand and customer expectations.

Ignoring Your Local Environment

In the Pacific Northwest, fog, clouds, and rain can mute colors. Bright white might look clinical and cold; muted tones can look muddy. That’s why color selection tailored to your region matters and why we always consider the PNW’s lighting and weather in our recommendations.

Your exterior is your visual handshake to every customer who passes by. Whether they realize it or not, they’re making assumptions about your service, quality, and trustworthiness based on what they see.
